reader.summary: Australian courts delivered a definitive verdict in the Erin Patterson mushroom poisoning case, rejecting her appeal and imposing a harsher sentence that bars her from ever being released. The story dominated headlines alongside a separate ruling that denied her the right to eat Vegemite in prison. In cricket, South Africa claimed a 2-1 series win over Australia, with Harmer posting a career-best 6-16 in the decider; Mitchell Starc's 6-72 sparked a late Australian recovery that fell short of the target. The economy showed strain as September inflation accelerated beyond forecasts ahead of an RBA meeting, while banks eased lending standards amid a property slump. Diplomatically, the Prime Minister is set to visit Beijing following the APEC summit, and the treasurer urged middle powers to cooperate beyond geopolitical rivalries. On the technology front, Australia's data-centre push gathered momentum with AirTrunk securing a $3 billion green loan and a 20-year power pact signed for the Pilgangoora mine. The US assigned its first nuclear-powered submarine to an Australian base, keeping AUKUS on track for early-2030s delivery. The Australian MotoGP Grand Prix was cancelled by rain at Phillip Island, and Star Entertainment accepted a $183.6 million anti-money-laundering penalty.

Here's what's happening in Australia right now. The courts just wrapped up a big case about a woman who poisoned people with mushrooms, and the banks just reported that inflation is getting worse. At the same time, the government is planning a trip to China to talk trade and resources.

Why does this matter? The central bank has to decide whether to raise or lower interest rates, and that affects everyone's mortgage and savings. The trip to China matters because China buys a lot of Australia's iron ore and other resources, and the two countries have had a rocky relationship lately.

What will probably happen next? The RBA will make its rate decision, and the PM will land in Beijing for talks. The data-centre buildout will keep generating news about power and investment.

What would be a surprise? If the government suddenly announces a big new rule about artificial intelligence, or if the Beijing visit produces an unexpected trade deal that shakes up the mining sector.

- South Africa vs Australia cricket (dominant, continuing): South Africa crushed Australia by an innings in the second Test to level the series 1-1, with Jansen taking five and Australia forced to follow on; selection headaches and a Smith injury complicate the Cape Town decider.

- Meta and social-media lawsuits (occasional, new): Meta faced an Australian class action over harm to children, and Australia moved to sue Facebook and TikTok for alleged breaches of a screen-time ban.

- Snowy Hydro cost blowout (occasional, new): The Snowy Hydro project's cost blew out to an estimated $18 billion, eleven times the original estimate.
